sources.title: Debian version ordering and epoch/upstream/revision structure
sources.confirmed: Debian compares epoch numerically, then upstream version and Debian revision using alternating non-digit and numeric runs; tilde sorts before the end of a string. It permits upstream version reformatting to fit distribution ordering.
sources.limits: Its character rules, tilde ordering and revision semantics require explicit translation from existing Python versions; the live page was not backdated to the cutoff. sources.title: RubyGems Gem::Version and Gem::Requirement
sources.sections_read: Version overview; prerelease ordering; dependency bounds
sources.confirmed: Gem::Version compares numeric components numerically and splits letters and digits in prereleases; prereleases precede the corresponding release. Gem::Requirement supplies compound bounds over these comparable objects.
sources.limits: RubyGems' supported syntax and prerelease interpretation need adaptation for arbitrary legacy version strings; current master documentation was not verified as pre-cutoff. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C31.json.

sources.title: Apache Ivy 2.1.0 LatestStrategy and dependency ranges
sources.version_or_date: Ivy 2.1.0 versioned documentation, dated by 2009-10-08 release announcement
sources.confirmed: Ivy offers pluggable revision comparators, including a semantic qualifier ordering with configurable special words; lexicographic and revision-date orderings are separate strategies.
sources.limits: Different comparator configurations must be shared consistently by producers and consumers; the separate date-based latest strategy does not solve semantic ordering when uploads occur out of order. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C31.json.

sources.title: Apache Maven ComparableVersion
sources.sections_read: Features; comparator API; canonical form; CLI example
sources.confirmed: ComparableVersion splits numbers, strings and separator transitions, orders known qualifiers, exposes comparison and canonicalization, and gives unknown qualifiers a defined order.
sources.limits: Maven assigns ecosystem-specific precedence to separators and qualifiers, so its order cannot be assumed to match legacy Python, Debian or RPM expectations; the opened API is live. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C31.json.

sources.title: Python distutils StrictVersion and LooseVersion
sources.version_or_date: CPython v2.6.4; official release dated October 25/26, 2009
sources.sections_read: Direct unauthenticated HTTP request: StrictVersion and LooseVersion parsing and comparison implementations
sources.confirmed: The tagged source returned HTTP 200 and implements StrictVersion with numeric tuples and alpha/beta prereleases, and LooseVersion with numeric and string token lists. Its comments explicitly describe legacy date formats and the prerelease-ordering limitation of loose tuple comparison.
sources.limits: StrictVersion accepts only two or three numeric components with optional alpha/beta tags; LooseVersion's tuple ordering can place a prerelease after its release, so accepting a string does not establish its intended order. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C31.json.
